description: I'm Jorge, a biologist and science teacher. With support from Colegio Milagros de Dios, my students and I formed Sinchi Rovers. We built ANEMOS to help rainfed maize growers use NASA rainfall records to see how often dry spells followed a chosen planting date.
summary: ANEMOS is a calendar for rainfed maize growers who rely on rainfall for germination and early crop establishment. A grower selects a location and taps a date to see how often a dry spell occurred in the following 30 days in past years. The calendar uses daily NASA GPM IMERG rainfall estimates and uses color to make the historical record easy to read. A documented case of uneven early maize growth in Caicay, Cusco, Peru, inspired the project.
details:
ANEMOS is a browser-based calendar for growers who rely on rain for germination and early crop establishment. On the welcome screen, choose “See the calendar,” select a location, and tap one date. The calendar reports how often a dry spell followed that date in the next 30 days in past years. It uses daily NASA GPM IMERG rainfall estimates obtained through NASA POWER. ANEMOS counts a year when its complete 30-day record contains at least seven consecutive days with less than 1 mm of rain per day.

A SENAMHI field report from Caicay, Cusco, Peru, inspired the project. The report documented uneven early growth of rainfed giant white maize associated with low soil moisture. ANEMOS puts daily satellite data into a familiar calendar, using color and a count of years to show dry spells that can be hidden by a rainfall total alone. The goal is to help growers use local rainfall history to decide what to check in their fields before sowing. The underlying satellite estimate represents the surrounding area, so field moisture and the local forecast also matter. The web application was built with JavaScript.

An optional “NASA map and data” section lets users explore the record in more detail. It shows the annual history and the trend in rainfall accumulated during the 30 days after the selected date. Estimated root-zone soil wetness, temperature, and solar radiation provide additional context for the location. The calendar’s dry-spell calculation uses daily rainfall alone. A grower can use the calendar directly from the welcome screen.

AI use disclosure: AI tools assisted with software development and preparation of the English submission materials. AI-generated visuals appear in ANEMOS and in the project demo. The demo narration is AI-generated and based on a real human voice.
